blocks.content: It shall be the duty of the Union Commission to present annually to the President a report as to the work done by the Commission.

items: UPSC submits its report to the President, NOT directly to the Parliament or the Prime Minister.
Non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be explicitly justified in a memorandum presented to Parliament.
Questions often confuse Article 320 (Functions of UPSC) with Article 323 (Reports of Public Service Commissions).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Under Article 323 of the Constitution, the UPSC submits an annual report on its performance to the President.
The President causes the report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
An explanatory memorandum must accompany the report, explaining cases where the advice of the Commission was not accepted and the reasons for such non-acceptance.
Individual ministries or departments cannot reject UPSC advice; rejection requires approval from the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
